crop.notes: Whole front-page article: portraits and records of Ryan and Sullivan, 'The Gladiators' review across several columns, and the short 'Ryan All O.K.' follow-up.

ocr.notes: Accurate as far as it goes, but the transcript stops partway through the Coburn paragraph ('his brother Mickey being a splendid lightweight fighter') and omits the rest, including every passage about Allen. Sullivan's fighting weight is 182 in the image, not 152; the 'Paudeen' sentence about Morrissey is dropped.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported Sullivan's nine-round win over Paddy Ryan and reviewed the American ring, including Allen's 1869 fights with Davis, Gallagher and McCoole and his 1870 loss to Jem Mace near New Orleans.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Wednesday, February 8, 1882, front page.

facts.fact: Allen came to America on the same voyage ('on one invoice') as Billy Ryall and Peter Morris, the English lightweight champion
In 1869 Allen beat Bill Davis, and Charley Gallagher beat Allen at Carroll Island near St. Louis
In June 1869 Allen and Mike McCoole met on an island (printed 'Boster's Island'); the fight was broken up after McCoole was well whipped
In August 1869 Allen beat Charley Gallagher badly in a rematch

Allen lost to Jem Mace at Kennerville near New Orleans in 1870 for $2,500 a side; Mace threw him in the tenth round, Allen was knocked insensible, Coburn threw up the sponge, and it was feared Allen's neck was broken
Allen seconded Jem Mace, with Jim Cusick, in Mace's drawn fight with Joe Coburn at Bay St. Louis on November 30, 1871
The paper said Allen could never have won his fight with Joe Goss under any circumstances, 'being robbed out of the battle'

notes: Mainly about Sullivan-Ryan; Allen appears in the historical review (crops 9-12). The retrospective is secondhand, so fight facts are medium confidence. The transcript should be completed from the image so that the Allen passages can be searched.
